newsitem.title: INDIA: India sugar ranged on low demand, limited arrivals.
newsitem.headline: India sugar ranged on low demand, limited arrivals.

text.p: Sugar prices held steady in a narrow price band on the local market on Friday on sluggish consumer demand though limited arrivals kept the market quiet, dealers said.
"Offtake remained slow during the day on account of heavy rain in the city and nearby areas," one broker said.

In the ready delivery sugar S-30 was quiet at 1,450/1,480 rupees per quintal as was sugar M-30 at 1,475/1,508 rupees per quintal. Volume was at low ebb as major players kept to the sidelines awaiting the announcement of the free sale quota by the Indian government for next month.
"The announcement is now overdue but the delay also reduced speculative interest in the market," he added.

Sugar mill delivery moved down on the absence of outstation buying at the mill level. In the mill delivery sugar S-30 slid by 5/15 rupees at 1,385/1,395 rupees per quintal while sugar M-30 fell by 10 rupees in the mill delivery at 1,405/1,425 rupees per quintal.
Free sale quota for the current month is 800,000 tonnes with traders' opinion divided over the expectation for July. Opinions range between 725,000 and 800,000 tonnes for July.
